O fundo da língua faz contato com a regi: The back of the tongue touches the back of the roof of the mouth, then releases. This is a plain consonant: its sound changes with its position in a word, so it is not always an English “g.”
A ponta da língua toca a região logo atr: The tongue tip touches the area just behind the upper teeth. Air flows through the nose: this is a nasal consonant, close to “n.”
A ponta da língua bloqueia o ar na regiã: The tongue tip blocks airflow behind the upper teeth, then releases. This is a plain consonant; do not assume it is an English “d” in every position.
Em muitas posições entre vogais, a ponta: In many positions between vowels, the tongue tip makes a brief tap behind the upper teeth. At the end of a syllable, the sound is different, closer to “l.” It is not the usual English “r.”
Feche os dois lábios e deixe o ar passar: Close both lips and let air flow through your nose. This is a nasal consonant, close to “m.”
Feche os lábios para bloquear o ar e dep: Close your lips to block the air, then release. This is the plain consonant in this family; it is not always an English “b.”
A língua se aproxima da região atrás dos: The tongue approaches the area behind the upper teeth, leaving a narrow passage for air. The friction is close to an “s” sound; before ㅣ, the sound quality changes.
No começo do bloco, ocupa a posição de c: At the beginning of a block, it fills the initial consonant position silently. At the end of a block, it sounds like “ng,” without releasing a separate “g.”
O som começa com um bloqueio e termina e: The sound begins with a closure and releases into friction, behind the upper teeth. This is the plain consonant in the ㅈ, ㅊ and ㅉ family.
Começa com bloqueio e termina em fricção: It begins with a closure and releases into friction, like the ㅈ family. A more noticeable puff of air accompanies the release: this is an aspirated consonant.
Use a região posterior da língua, como e: Use the back of the tongue, as in ㄱ, but release it with a more noticeable puff of air. This is the aspirated consonant in the family.
Use a região atrás dos dentes superiores: Use the area behind the upper teeth, as in ㄷ, with a more noticeable puff of air at release. This is an aspirated consonant.
Os lábios se fecham e se abrem com um so: The lips close and release with a more noticeable puff of air than in the plain member of the family. This is aspirated; it is not an English “f.”
Há passagem de ar na glote, na região da: Air passes through the glottis, in the throat. At the beginning of 하, you hear breath; do not confuse this with silent initial ㅇ.
Uma soltura sem exagerar o sopro nem a t: Release without exaggerating the puff of air or muscular tension. The sound depends on position and context; it does not exactly match an English consonant.
A soltura vem acompanhada de um sopro ma: A more noticeable puff of air accompanies the release. Aspiration describes this airflow, not an extra vowel after the consonant.
O início do som é mais firme e compacto,: The onset is firmer and more compact, without adding the puff of the aspirated sound. This does not mean shouting or saying the consonant twice.

O Hangul foi criado pelo rei Sejong, na: King Sejong created Hangul in 1443, during Korea’s Joseon dynasty, and introduced it publicly in 1446. Originally called Hunminjeongeum, it was designed to make reading and writing more accessible at a time when Chinese characters were used.

No Hangul, o alfabeto coreano, cada bloc: In Hangul, the Korean alphabet, each block represents one syllable. A written block must have a consonant in the initial position and a vowel. These are its two essential parts; it may also have a final consonant.
E quando a sílaba começa com som de voga: What if a syllable starts with a vowel sound? The initial position is still required in writing. This is where the consonant ㅇ comes in: at the start of a block, it is silent and adds no sound. In 아, for example, we write ㅇ + ㅏ but hear only the vowel.

그럴 = fazer isso, de 그러다; 수 있다 = poder; -: 그럴, from 그러다, refers to doing so; 수 있다 expresses ability, narrowed by -만; -다면 introduces a hypothetical. 물어보다 means to ask, and -고 싶었어 describes a past wish.

나에겐 = 나에게는, quanto a mim; 이름이 = nome com: 나에겐 contracts 나에게는, as for me; 이름이 marks name as the subject. 없구나 registers the discovery of an absence. This is the hurt speaker’s perspective, not a literal astronomical naming claim.

나도 = eu também; 너의 = seu; 별 pode designa: 나도 means me too; 너의 means your. 별 can poetically refer to a celestial body without requiring a scientific star. -이었는데 sets a past state against what followed.

넌 = 너는; 빛 = luz; -이라서 dá a razão com um: 넌 is 너는; 빛 means light. -이라서 supplies a reason after a noun; 좋겠다 imagines that something must be nice, with bitterness here.
Enquanto eu apenas recebo essa luz que v: While all I do is receive that light from you.
난 = 나는; 그런 널 = você desse jeito, retoman: 난 is 나는; 그런 널 refers to you in that role as light. 받을 뿐 means only receive; -인데 contrasts the positions. The translation makes the image explicit without changing 받다 into reflect.
무너진 vem de 무너지다, desmoronar, e modifica: 무너진 comes from 무너지다, to collapse, and modifies 왕성, royal castle; -에 locates the scene. The sentence continues into the next line.
Que sentido tem a vida que ainda resta?: What meaning is there in the life that remains?
남은 = que restou; 명 aqui é vida ou tempo: 남은 means remaining; 명 here refers to life or one’s remaining lifespan. 뭔 contracts 무슨; 의미가 있어 asks what meaning there is. Name and life echo through the verse’s imagery.
Acho que vou receber até morrer: I suppose I will keep receiving, until I die,
죽을 때까지 = até o momento de morrer; 받겠지 co: 죽을 때까지 means until the time I die; 받겠지 combines receiving with expectation or supposition. Its object comes in the following line.
니 é a forma coloquial usada na letra par: 니 is the colloquial spelling used here for your, standard 네; 무더운 comes from 무덥다, oppressively hot; 시선 means gaze. The heat contrasts with the frozen heart later.
Ainda orbito você e nada mudou, mas…: I still orbit you, and nothing has changed, but…
아직 = ainda; 널 돌고 = girando ao seu redor;: 아직 means still; 널 돌고 means orbiting you. 변한 건 contracts 변한 것은, what has changed; 없지만 denies change and introduces a contrast. 돌다 here means orbit, not simply turn a corner.
Se o amor não tem mais um nome,: If love no longer has a name,
사랑에 = no amor ou para esse amor; 이름이 = n: 사랑에 frames love as the domain; 이름이 marks name as the subject. 없다면 means if there is none, setting up the next conclusion.
모든 게 = 모든 것이, tudo; 변한 거야 apresenta o fa: 모든 게 contracts 모든 것이, everything; 변한 거야 presents the fact of having changed as a conclusion or explanation.
정말로 = realmente; Eris를 é o nome próprio: 정말로 means really; Eris를 marks the proper name as object. 찾아내다 means to discover or find after a search; -ㄴ 걸까 forms a wondering question. The reference can suggest a replacement within the metaphor.
Me diga: em que sou inferior àquela lua?: Tell me: how am I any less than that moon?
말해 = diga, informal; 내가 = eu como sujeit: 말해 is the informal tell me; 내가 marks I as subject. 저 달보다 compares with that moon; 못하다 here means to be inferior; 게 뭐야 asks in what respect.
-는 põe Us como tópico; u의 = de u; 복수형 =: -는 makes Us the topic; u의 means of u; 복수형 means plural form; -일 뿐 means is only. This is visual and emotional wordplay with u/you and us, not a rule of English grammar.
Talvez eu nunca tenha estado ali, desde: Maybe I was never there in the first place.
어쩌면 = talvez; 거기 = ali; 처음부터 = desde o c: 어쩌면 means maybe; 거기 means there; 처음부터 means from the beginning. 없었던 거야 frames a past absence as the speaker’s present interpretation.
Um dia você também vai entender estas pa: Someday you will understand these words too, won’t you?
언젠가 = algum dia; 너도 = você também; 이 말을: 언젠가 means someday; 너도 means you too; 이 말을 marks these words as the object. 이해하겠지 expresses an expectation of understanding, not an absolute guarantee.
Todas as minhas estações sempre foram vo: You were always every season of my life.
나의 계절은 = minhas estações como tópico; 언제: 나의 계절은 makes my seasons the topic; 언제나 means always; 너였어 means were you. Seasons image the speaker’s time and life organized around the other person.
Meu coração gelado está a 248 graus abai: My cold heart is 248 degrees below zero.
내 = meu; 차가운 = frio; 심장은 = coração como: 내 means my; 차가운 means cold; 심장은 makes heart the topic; 영하 means below zero; 도 means degrees. The number belongs to the coldness metaphor, not a universal fixed temperature for Pluto.
It stopped on the day you erased me.
니가 = você como sujeito, padrão 네가; 날 = 나: 니가 marks you as subject, standard 네가; 날 is 나를. 지운 modifies 그 날, the day you erased me; 멈췄어 is the past of 멈추다. The heart carries over from the previous line.
I just keep circling around you.
맴돌다 = circular ao redor; -고 있다 = ação em: 맴돌다 means to circle around; -고 있다 marks an ongoing action; -만 restricts it to nothing else. Repetition reinforces being trapped in this emotional orbit.
(Eu deixei você escapar, eu perdi você.): (I let you slip away; I lost you.)
놓쳤어 vem de 놓치다, perder a chance ou deixa: 놓쳤어 comes from 놓치다, to miss or let slip away; 잃었어 comes from 잃다, to lose someone or something. The two verbs approach loss from different angles.
I just keep spinning in vain.
헛돌다 é girar sem produzir resultado, como: 헛돌다 means to turn without achieving anything, like a wheel spinning uselessly; -고만 있어 prolongs that futile action. It echoes 맴돌다 but adds frustration.
넌 = 너는; 날 = 나를; 지우다 = apagar; 잊다 = esque: 넌 is 너는; 날 is 나를; 지우다 means erase; 잊다 means forget. The similar sounds of 지웠어 and 잊었어 layer two images of exclusion.
Que um dia pertenceu ao mundo do Sol,: That once belonged to the Sun’s world,
한때는 = em outro tempo; 태양의 세계에 = ao mundo: 한때는 means once; 태양의 세계에 means to the Sun’s world. 속했던 modifies 별 in the next line; -았/었던 recalls a past state. Read across the line break.
(A canção parou, a canção cessou.): (The song stopped; the song fell silent.)
노랜 = 노래는, a canção como tópico; 멈추다 = pa: 노랜 contracts 노래는, making the song the topic; 멈추다 means stop; 멎다 means cease, as a sound or flow does. The second verb deepens the silence.
No coração desse astro, só resta uma cam: In that celestial body’s heart, only a stifling layer of haze remains.
별의 = do astro; 심장엔 = 심장에는, no coração; 텁: 별의 means of the celestial body; 심장엔 contracts 심장에는, in its heart. 텁텁한 evokes a heavy, stuffy sensation; 안개층 means layer of haze; 뿐 means only. The final copula is left implicit.
지웠어 = apagou, de 지우다; 잊었어 = esqueceu, de: 지웠어 means erased, from 지우다; 잊었어 means forgot, from 잊다. The parenthetical response keeps the voice of loss beneath the astronomical image.
It is not so different from yesterday, ay.
어제와는 = em comparação com ontem; 그리 com n: 어제와는 compares with yesterday; 그리 with a negative means not so; 다를 건 means what would be different; 없네 observes that there is none.
Na rotina idêntica, só você não está, ay: In the same old routine, you are the only thing missing, ay.
똑같은 = exatamente igual; 일상 속에 = dentro d: 똑같은 means exactly the same; 일상 속에 means in everyday life; 딱 emphasizes just or exactly; 너만 means only you; 없네 notices the absence.
Até ontem, nós claramente estávamos junt: We were definitely together until yesterday, ay.
분명 = claramente; 어제까지는 = até ontem, com: 분명 means definitely; 어제까지는 contrasts until yesterday with now; 함께였는데 means we were together, but… The turn comes in the next line.
Num dia assustadoramente igual, só você: In a day so unchanged it is frightening, only you are missing.
무서울 정도로 = a ponto de assustar; 하루 속엔 = 하: 무서울 정도로 means to a frightening degree; 하루 속엔 contracts 하루 속에는, within the day. 딱 너만 없네 repeats that only the other person is missing.
Para ser sincero, naquele ano mais ou me: Honestly, during that year or so without you,
솔직히 말해 = falando honestamente; 니가 없던 mod: 솔직히 말해 means honestly speaking; 니가 없던 modifies 일년쯤, a year or so without you. Standard spacing is 일 년쯤; the sentence continues.
Eu estava indiferente; nem aquele apego: I felt unaffected; even that lingering attachment people talk about
덤덤했지 = eu estava indiferente ou sereno;: 덤덤했지 recalls feeling unaffected or composed; 흔히 말하는 means commonly talked about; 미련도 means even lingering attachment. -도 belongs with the negation in the next line.
Existia naqueles dias; agora, quase esqu: Was there in those days; now, it has almost slipped my mind…
없던 fecha 미련도, nem havia apego; 지난 날 = di: 없던 completes 미련도: there was not even lingering attachment; 지난 날 means past days; 이젠 is 이제는, now; 깜빡 suggests a lapse of memory. The claim of indifference becomes unstable in what follows.
Nem lembro mais do seu perfume nem nada: I do not even remember your scent anymore—wait.
니 향기 = seu perfume; 따윈 = 따위는, coisas com: 니 향기 means your scent; 따윈 contracts 따위는, dismissively things like that; 기억도 안 나 means I do not even remember; 잠깐 means wait. The pause undercuts the confident claim.
Mas é um perfume que já senti em algum l: But this is a scent I have smelled somewhere before, ay.
근데 = mas; 어디선가 = em algum lugar; 맡아봤던 co: 근데 means but; 어디선가 means somewhere; 맡아봤던 combines smelling with a remembered experience; 향순데 contracts 향수인데, it is a perfume, and… Recognition begins.
Quando a lembrança começa a florescer va: As a vague memory starts to bloom, ay,
기억이 = lembrança como sujeito; 어렴풋이 = vag: 기억이 marks memory as subject; 어렴풋이 means vaguely; 피어나다 means bloom or emerge; -(으)ㄹ 즈음에 means around the time when, written 즘에 here.
Ali, ali — quando viro a cabeça para olh: Over there, over there—when I turn to look,
저기 = ali; 고개를 = cabeça como objeto; 돌려보니: 저기 means over there; 고개를 marks the head as object; 돌려보니 means upon turning to look, I discover. -니 links the action to the discovery that follows.
Ao seu lado, enquanto você se aproxima s: Beside you, as you approach with a bright smile, is that person…
환하게 = radiantemente; 웃으며 = sorrindo; 다가오: 환하게 means brightly; 웃으며 means smiling; 다가오는 modifies 니, you as you approach; 옆엔 is 옆에는, beside. 그... leaves the other person unnamed in a hesitation.
안녕 é uma saudação informal. As duas voze: 안녕 is an informal greeting. The two voices stage an ordinary encounter in contrast with the speaker’s inner response.
How have you been? Me? Oh, I am doing fine.
어떻게 지내? = como tem passado?; 나는 = quanto: 어떻게 지내? asks how someone has been; 나는 shifts the topic to me; 뭐 is a conversational filler or understatement; 잘 지내 means I am doing fine. The ordinary reply contrasts with the next line’s heart.
Diferente do meu coração, que parece pre: Unlike my heart, which somehow feels ready to burst,
왠지 = por algum motivo; 터질 듯한 = que parec: 왠지 means for some reason; 터질 듯한 means seemingly about to burst, written together here; 심장과는 달리 means unlike my heart. The comparison is completed by the scene’s temperature.
A temperatura deste instante é de 248 ab: This moment’s temperature is 248 below zero.
이 순간 = este instante; 온도는 = temperatura: 이 순간 means this moment; 온도는 makes temperature the topic; 영하 means below zero. The returning number describes an emotionally frozen encounter.
(Além da névoa, ainda observo você sorri: (Beyond the haze, I still watch you smiling,
안개 너머의 = além da névoa, com ligação nomi: 안개 너머의 points beyond the haze in a poetic noun linkage; 여전히 means still; 미소 띤 means wearing a smile; 널 지켜보지 means I watch you. The parenthesis continues into the next line.
A realidade da minha órbita irregular, s: The reality of my irregular orbit, with neither meaning nor you.)
의미도, 너도, 다 없는 = em que faltam tanto sent: 의미도, 너도, 다 없는 means lacking both meaning and you; 불규칙 means irregularity, compressed poetically here; 내 궤도의 현실 means the reality of my orbit. The poetic order concentrates the loss of an anchor.
(Para você, um número difícil de lembrar: (To you, a number hard to remember and a Pluto in darkness;
너에겐 = 너에게는, para você; 기억하기 힘든 = difícil: 너에겐 is 너에게는, to you; 기억하기 힘든 means hard to remember; 숫자 means number; 어둠의 means of darkness. The numerical title gains meaning through the gaze that no longer recognizes the speaker.
Mesmo assim, vou continuar girando ao se: Even so, I suppose I will keep circling around you, damn.)
그래도 = mesmo assim; 계속 = continuamente; 너: 그래도 means even so; 계속 means continually; 너의 주위를 means around you; 맴돌겠지 anticipates continuing to orbit. The concession does not undo the loss.
마라톤 = maratona, empréstimo. A repetição: 마라톤 is the loanword marathon. Repetition introduces life as a race before questioning the obligation to run.
Life is long; take it slowly.
삶은 = vida como tópico; 길어 = é longa, de: 삶은 makes life the topic; 길어 means is long, from 길다; 천천히 means slowly; 해 is the informal do or take it.
Dizem que no fim está um paraíso cheio d: They promise a paradise full of dreams at the finish.
그 끝엔 = 그 끝에는, naquele fim; 꿈의 낙원 = paraí: 그 끝엔 contracts 그 끝에는, at that end; 꿈의 낙원 means paradise of dreams; 가득해 means is full. The translation brings out the promise that the following contrast questions.
하지만 = mas; 진짜 = real, verdadeiro; 세상은 =: 하지만 means but; 진짜 means real; 세상은 makes world the topic. Read into the next line.
Is different from what was promised.
약속 = promessa; -과는 달라 = é diferente de,: 약속 means promise; -과는 달라 means is different from, with a topic contrast. It does not mean a scheduled appointment here.
We have to run, have to keep pushing.
우린 = 우리는; 달려야 해 = temos que correr; 밟아야: 우린 contracts 우리는; 달려야 해 means have to run; 밟아야 해 means have to step or press down. -아/어야 하다 expresses obligation. The compressed image conveys pressure to advance without naming an object for 밟다.
Quando disparam o sinal de largada,: When the starting signal is fired,
신호탄을 = sinalizador ou tiro de sinal como: 신호탄을 marks a signal flare or shot as object; 쏘면 means if or when it is fired, from 쏘다. The race context gives it the sense of a starting signal.
You do not even have a destination.
너 = você, destacado; 목적지 = destino; -도 c: 너 means you, singled out; 목적지 means destination; -도 with 없어 means not even. Having no destination makes the demand to run contradictory.
There is no scenery at all.
아무 풍경도 없어 = não há qualquer paisagem; 아무: 아무 풍경도 없어 means there is no scenery at all; 아무…도 with a negative excludes every possibility. Running leaves no room to notice the journey.
Quando o fôlego já chega ao limite,: When you are completely out of breath,
숨이 = fôlego como sujeito; 턱까지 = até o qu: 숨이 marks breath as subject; 턱까지 literally reaches the chin; 넘치다 means overflow; -ㄹ 때 means when. The bodily image conveys extreme breathlessness.
Você precisa, você precisa…: You need to, you need to…
멈춰서다 = parar de avançar; -아/어도 = mesmo q: 멈춰서다 means to come to a stop; -아/어도 means even if; 괜찮아 means it is okay. The concession allows a pause without framing it as failure.
Não precisa correr sem nem saber por quê: You do not need to run without even knowing why.
아무 이유도 모르는 채 = sem conhecer motivo algum: 아무 이유도 모르는 채 means without knowing any reason; -(으)ㄴ 채 keeps a state in place during an action; 달릴 필요 없어 means there is no need to run. -ㄹ 필요 없다 denies necessity.
It is okay not to have a grand dream.
꿈이 = sonho como sujeito; 없어도 = mesmo que: 꿈이 marks dream as subject; 없어도 means even if you do not have one; 괜찮아 means it is okay. Grand brings out the ambitious ideal demanded in context; 꿈 itself can also mean an ordinary dream.
Se você tiver momentos seus para sentir: If you have moments of your own to feel a little happiness.
잠시 = por um momento; 행복을 느낄 modifica 네 순: 잠시 means for a moment; 행복을 느낄 modifies 네 순간들, your moments of feeling happiness; 있다면 means if there are any. The condition values present experience.
멈춰서도 = mesmo que pare; 괜찮아 = tudo bem. A: 멈춰서도 means even if you stop; 괜찮아 means it is okay. Repetition counters the pressure to keep going at any cost.
Agora não corro mais sem nem saber o obj: Now I no longer run without even knowing the purpose.
이젠 = 이제는, agora; 목적 = propósito, diferen: 이젠 contracts 이제는, now; 목적 means purpose, unlike 목적지, destination; 모르는 채 means without knowing; 달리지 않아 means I do not run. Permission becomes a new stance.
-이 없어도 괜찮아 combina ausência e concessão:: -이 없어도 괜찮아 combines absence with concession: even without it, it is okay. The line does not forbid dreams; it removes the requirement of a grand ambition.
Every breath you breathe is already in paradise.
네가 = você como sujeito da oração que mod: 네가 is the subject inside the clause modifying 호흡; 내뱉는 means exhaling; 모든 호흡은 makes every breath the topic; 이미 means already; 낙원에 means in paradise, with the verb of being left implicit.
Tomamos sonhos emprestados dos outros, c: We borrow our dreams from others, like debts.
우린 = 우리는; 꿈을 = sonhos como objeto; 남한테서: 우린 is 우리는; 꿈을 marks dreams as object; 남한테서 means from others. 꿔 plays on 꾸다, to dream, and 꾸다, to borrow. 빚처럼, like debt, makes the second reading explicit.
Aprendemos que temos de ser grandiosos,: We are taught that we must become great, like light.
위대해지다 = tornar-se grandioso; -어야 한다 = de: 위대해지다 means become great; -어야 한다 means must; 배워 means learn. 빛처럼 means like light and sounds close to 빚처럼, like debt, in the preceding line.
Your dream is actually a burden.
너의 = seu; 사실은 = na verdade; 짐 = bagagem: 너의 means your; 사실은 means actually; 짐 means baggage or burden. The sound shift from dream to 짐 turns an imposed aspiration into something you must carry.
Se só o futuro conta como sonho,: If only the future counts as a dream,
미래 = futuro; -만이 restringe o sujeito: só: 미래 means future; -만이 restricts the subject to only that; 꿈이라면 means if it is a dream. The hypothetical prepares the contrast between aspiration and a dream during sleep.
Então o que foi aquilo que sonhei ontem: Then what was it I dreamed in bed last night?
내가 = eu; 어젯밤 = ontem à noite; 침대서 = 침대에서: 내가 means I; 어젯밤 means last night; 침대서 contracts 침대에서, in bed; 꾼 건 is 꾼 것은, what I dreamed; 뭐 means what. Here 꾸다 means dreaming during sleep.
Tudo bem se o seu sonho tiver outro nome: It is okay for your dream to have a different name.
꿈의 이름이 = nome do sonho como sujeito; 달라도: 꿈의 이름이 marks the dream’s name as subject; 달라도 means even if it differs, from 다르다; 괜찮아 means it is okay. It makes room for less grand desires.
다음 달에 = no próximo mês, aqui unido; 노트북: 다음 달에 means next month, written together here; 노트북 means laptop; 사는 거 turns buying into a named activity or desire.
아니면 = ou então; 그냥 = simplesmente; 먹고 자다: 아니면 means or else; 그냥 means simply; 먹고 자다 links eating and sleeping; -는 거 turns the activity into a noun phrase.
Having plenty of money without doing anything.
암것도 = 아무것도, nada sob negação; 안 하는데 = se: 암것도 is colloquial 아무것도, nothing under negation; 안 하는데 means not doing anything, but; 돈이 많은 거 names the state of having plenty of money. The tone is casual and humorous.
Como se sonho precisasse ser uma coisa g: As if a dream has to be something grand.
꿈이 = sonho como sujeito; 뭐 aqui dá tom d: 꿈이 marks dream as subject; 뭐 adds a challenging tone; 거창한 거 means something grand; -라고 echoes an idea to question it in an elliptical conversational phrase.
그냥 = simplesmente; 아무나 = qualquer pessoa: 그냥 means simply; 아무나 means anyone; 되라고 reports an instruction to be or become. In context it challenges the duty to become someone exceptional rather than belittling the listener.
Seja grande ou pequeno, você continua se: Big or small, you are still you.
뭐가 = seja o que for; 크건 작건 = seja grande: 뭐가 means whatever it may be; 크건 작건 means whether big or small, using -건…-건; 너는 너잖어 means you are you, after all. -잖어 is colloquial -잖아, appealing to shared recognition.
Sometimes having a dream is frightening.
꿈을 꾸는 게 = sonhar como sujeito, de 것이; 때론: 꿈을 꾸는 게 makes dreaming the subject, contracting 것이; 때론 is 때로는, sometimes; 무섭네 observes that it is frightening.
Simplesmente continuar vivendo assim,: Simply going on living like this,
그냥 = simplesmente; 이렇게 = assim; 살아가다 = s: 그냥 means simply; 이렇게 means like this; 살아가다 means to go on living; -는 게 makes the action the subject. The sentence continues.
Sobreviver — para mim, esse já é um pequ: Surviving—that is already a small dream for me.
살아남다 = sobreviver; 이게 = 이것이, isto; 나에겐 =: 살아남다 means survive; 이게 is 이것이, this; 나에겐 is 나에게는, for me; 작은 꿈인데 means it is a small dream, but… Even a modest wish deserves room.
Sonhar, segurar um sonho,: Dreaming, holding on to a dream,
꿈을 꾸다 = sonhar; 꿈을 쥐다 = agarrar um sonho: 꿈을 꾸다 means dream; 꿈을 쥐다 means grasp a dream. The shift from 꾸다 to 쥐다 moves from imagining to trying to hold the dream in your hands.
Às vezes, até respirar é difícil de supo: Sometimes even breathing feels like too much.
숨을 쉬다 = respirar; -는 게 nomeia a ação; 때론: 숨을 쉬다 means breathe; -는 게 names the action; 때론 means sometimes; 버겁다 means to feel beyond one’s capacity or hard to bear. The line describes the speaker’s experience without making a diagnosis.
Dizendo que fulano vive assim e outro vi: Saying that one person lives this way and another lives that way,
누군 = 누구는, alguém como tópico contrastivo: 누군 contracts 누구는, someone as a contrasting topic; 이렇게 and 저렇게 mean this way and that way; 산다면서 reports talk used to compare lives.
The world showers me with insults.
세상은 = mundo como tópico; 내게 = em mim ou: 세상은 makes the world the topic; 내게 means at me; 욕을 marks insults as object; 퍼붓다 means pour out in quantity; -네 registers the experience.
The world has no right to insult you.
욕할 modifica 자격, direito ou legitimidade: 욕할 modifies 자격, the right or standing to insult; 자격이 없다 denies that standing. The target of 욕하다 is supplied by context.
꿈을 꾸는 법 = maneira de sonhar; -이 무엇인지 = o: 꿈을 꾸는 법 means how to dream; -이 무엇인지 embeds the question of what it is. This line is the object of teaching in the next sentence.
Because it has never even taught us how.
가르쳐 주다 = ensinar a alguém; -(으)ㄴ 적도 없다 =: 가르쳐 주다 means teach someone; -(으)ㄴ 적도 없다 means never even to have done something; -기에 supplies the reason. The world remains the subject.
Por ser um sonho inventado, vira um fala: Because it is a fabricated dream, it becomes tearful sleep-talk.
꾸며 내다 = inventar ou fabricar; 꿈이기에 = por: 꾸며 내다 means invent or fabricate; 꿈이기에 means because it is a dream; 눈물의 means of tears; 잠꼬대 means sleep-talk. The copula is elliptical; distinguish 꾸미다 from 꾸다, to dream.
I wake you from that nightmare, for your sake.

A música interrompe a sedução para falar: The song interrupts seduction to discuss watching videos, looking at photos and interpreting music videos. It is irony about the very content attracting the fan: the voice says to study, then invites them to listen again. The exaggeration of vanishing time reinforces this tension without literally measuring screen use.
상, prêmio, prepara o contraste com 벌, pu: 상, reward, prepares the contrast with 벌, punishment. 착해 sounds like praise for following the voice, and the pre-chorus insists there is no punishment. These choices maintain ambiguity between affection, play and control in the singing persona.
The title recalls the Pied Piper of Hamelin. In Robert Browning’s literary version, the piper’s music makes rats and later children follow him. The song reuses the pull of sound to build a seductive voice; that does not make the speaker a literal portrait of the story’s character.
선악과 nomeia o fruto do conhecimento do be: 선악과 names the fruit of the knowledge of good and evil, associated with Genesis. The comparison emphasizes attraction despite knowing there is a prohibition. The lyrics do not identify a fruit species; translating it as apple would add something the line does not say.
Salvar e arruinar ocupam a mesma constru: Saving and ruining occupy the same purpose construction. Repetition puts comfort and risk side by side rather than choosing a single simple meaning for the voice. Sweetness, guilty pleasure and the request for forgiveness extend that tension.
A lâmina primeiro é afiada todos os dias: The blade is first sharpened daily by ambition, then grows dull before desire the speaker cannot restrain. Later, reality itself cuts and tears. The image turns an instrument of determination into vulnerability.
저버리다 é abandonar, trair ou deixar de hon: 저버리다 means abandon, betray or fail to honor something, here one’s conscience. Its spelling resembles 져 버리다, end up losing, but the constructions differ. The postponed object identifies what was abandoned and helps prevent confusing the verbs.
A frase anterior diz que o eu não tinha: The preceding line says the speaker had not imagined; this one completes what was not foreseen. The trumpet summoning hell magnifies desire’s consequence. It works within the lyrics’ field of devil, guilt and temptation without requiring a specific scene to be assigned to it.

O eu reconhece a ameaça e ainda assim nã: The speaker recognizes the threat yet still does not want to lose the touch. The English chorus maintains the same contradiction between bad and sweet. The final repetition names evil without erasing the conflict the voice has just narrated.

Ponte do outro · uma escolha sem arrepen: Outro bridge · a choice without regret
Extra pode ser figurante, alguém que não: Extra can mean a background performer, someone outside the center of the scene. Joined to ordinary, it forms extraordinary. The wordplay turns being underestimated into the possibility of taking a leading role.
지다 pode ter sentidos diferentes conforme: 지다 can mean different things by context: a flower can fade or fall; a person can lose a contest. With 꽃, the immediate image is a flower’s ending. The introduction about losing allows a resonance between the meanings without making them identical.
A sequência troca voar por correr, camin: The sequence replaces flying with running, walking and crawling. Resistance does not depend on sustaining the same speed or ability: it finds another way to keep going. The compressed conditions should not be copied as neutral explanatory prose.
기어 vem de 기다, rastejar, e se aproxima do: 기어 comes from 기다, to crawl, and sounds close to English gear. The lyric uses that sound bridge to move from physical action to getting ready. Waiting is 기다리다: the similar beginning does not make the two verbs the same.
The two negatives do different jobs. The first commands someone not to kneel; the second states that there is no crying. Their parallel sound does not erase the difference between a prohibition and a declaration.
O teto de vidro é uma metáfora para barr: A glass ceiling is a metaphor for hard-to-see barriers that prevent advancement. The term has a history of describing obstacles faced by women and minorities at work; here the lyric places it within the broader call to underdogs. The barrier is not a physical ceiling.
방탄 é parte do nome coreano do BTS e tamb: 방탄 is part of BTS’s Korean name and also means bulletproof. The lyric connects that identity with the language of resistance and the collective refrain. Its meaning is an image of unity and persistence.
A pena pequena vira asa na lembrança inf: A small feather becomes a wing in the childhood memory; later, back pain is explained as growing wings. The image connects a modest beginning, difficulty and growth, without claiming that every real pain has that cause.
A frase contém duas vozes: alguém diz nã: The sentence contains two voices: someone says do not go, and the speaker takes that path. The negative command sits inside the modifier of the noun path. Separating the quoted voice from the main action avoids translating the line as though the speaker were forbidding the journey.
미약 fala de algo fraco ou pequeno; 비약 é u: 미약 describes something weak or slight; 비약 is a leap or advance. Their similar sounds help turn present smallness into momentum toward a grand ending. The preceding ending concedes difficulty rather than denying it.
걸 nem sempre tem a mesma função. Nesta l: 걸 does not always do the same job. In this line, it shortens 것을 and makes what one must not want an object. In endings such as the first flight, the construction explains something; in the anticipated leap, the ending expresses expectation. Read the whole sentence before assigning the form one fixed meaning.
